newsitem.title: INDIA: India to supply cheap grains to 350 million poor.
newsitem.headline: India to supply cheap grains to 350 million poor.

text.p: The Indian cabinet approved a proposal on Friday to provide subsidised foodgrains to an estimated 350 million poor people at half the market price, the United News of India (UNI) said.

The news agency said 66 million families, identified as living below the "poverty line" in the nation with an estimated population of 930 million, would benefit from a welfare scheme scheduled to take effect from January 26.
Each poor family falling in the category would be entitled to 10 kg (22 lbs) of foodgrains at subsidised rates every month, UNI said.
There was no immediate official confirmation of the report, and it was not clear how much it would cost the exchequer.
The poverty line is an economic concept used to identify those people whose incomes are so low they cannot afford two square meals a day.
Prime Minister H. D. Deve Gowda's centre-left United Front coalition that came to power last June had promised to provide foodgrains at concessional rates through government-controlled ration shops.
India observes January 26, the day marking the implementation of the republican constitution in 1950, as Republic Day.
